headline: Steady revenue but restructuring costs squeeze GAAP profit
summary_short: Q2 FY2026 net revenue was $14.4B, up 9.0% y/y (per the release) but essentially flat q/q, while GAAP diluted EPS fell to $0.49 (-15.5% q/q) as restructuring and other charges jumped to $365M from $126M in Q1; non-GAAP diluted EPS rose to $0.86, up 21.1% y/y.
summary_long: Personal Systems revenue grew 13% y/y to $10.2B on AI-PC demand; Printing was flat at $4.2B as unit declines were offset by pricing/supplies mix. GAAP diluted EPS of $0.49 missed HP's $0.52-$0.58 Q2 outlook and fell 15.5% q/q, driven by restructuring and other charges (including new CEO-transition costs) rising to $365M from $126M in Q1. Non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.86 beat the $0.70-$0.76 outlook by excluding those charges. HP generated $0.8B of free cash flow and returned $374M to shareholders via dividends and buybacks; gross cash ended at $3.7B. For Q3 FY2026, HP guides GAAP EPS of $0.47-$0.63, non-GAAP EPS of $0.61-$0.71; FY2026 GAAP EPS was updated to $2.15-$2.45, non-GAAP to $2.90-$3.10, FCF to $2.8-$3.0B.

drivers.explanation: 9% y/y growth (6.3% constant currency) led by Personal Systems +13% (Commercial PS +14%, Consumer PS +10%) on AI-PC demand; Printing was flat as unit declines were offset by supplies and pricing mix.

Sequential decline reflects restructuring and other charges rising to $365M from $126M in Q1, including new CEO-transition costs, even as total segment earnings before taxes rose slightly q/q ($1.27B vs $1.25B).

Same restructuring/CEO-transition cost step-up drove the q/q decline; GAAP EPS of $0.49 also missed the company's own $0.52-$0.58 Q2 outlook, while non-GAAP EPS of $0.86 beat its $0.70-$0.76 outlook by excluding those charges.

Q/q expansion is arithmetic: cost of net revenue fell 1.8% q/q ($11.39B vs $11.60B) while revenue was roughly flat, widening gross profit even though the release gives no qualitative driver for this line.

Company frames the quarter around AI-PC, edge-AI and HP IQ momentum, cites 'strong second-quarter results' with discipline in a dynamic environment, and updated (not explicitly stated as raised) FY2026 EPS and free-cash-flow ranges.
